What is the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS)?

The Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) is a mandatory pension scheme established under the Pension Reform Act 2014. Under this scheme, employers and employees contribute a minimum of 10% and 8% respectively of the employee's monthly emoluments into the employee's Retirement Savings Account (RSA).
How do I open a Retirement Savings Account (RSA)?

To open an RSA, visit any licensed Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) of your choice with a valid means of identification (National ID, Driver's License, or International Passport), passport photographs, and your Bank Verification Number (BVN). The PFA will issue you a PIN and account number.
Can I transfer my RSA to another PFA?

Yes. The Pension Reform Act allows RSA holders to transfer their accounts from one PFA to another once every year. To initiate a transfer, visit your chosen PFA and complete the RSA Transfer Application Form.
What is the Personal Pension Plan (PPP)?

The Personal Pension Plan (PPP) is a voluntary pension arrangement for self-employed individuals and workers in the informal sector. Contributions are flexible and determined by the contributor, with a minimum contribution of N500 per month.
When can I access my pension benefits?

You can access your retirement benefits upon reaching the age of 50 years and retiring from active employment. Benefits may also be accessed in cases of mental incapacity, terminal illness, or loss of employment before age 50 (with conditions).
What is a Pension Clearance Certificate (PCC)?

A Pension Clearance Certificate is a document issued by PenCom to employers confirming compliance with the Pension Reform Act. It is required for employers bidding for government contracts, accessing tax incentives, and participating in public procurement processes.

The Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) is a mandatory pension scheme established under the Pension Reform Act 2014. Under CPS, employers contribute 10% and employees contribute 8% of monthly emoluments into the employee's Retirement Savings Account (RSA). The scheme ensures you have savings for retirement.

A Retirement Savings Account (RSA) is your personal pension account. To open one, visit any licensed Pension Fund Administrator (PFA) with your National ID, passport photos, and BVN. You can choose any of the 22 licensed PFAs in Nigeria. Once opened, you'll receive a unique PIN.

Yes, you can transfer your RSA to another PFA once every year. Visit your chosen PFA, complete the RSA Transfer Form, and they will handle the process. PenCom will process the transfer within 3-5 working days. Your account balance and contribution history transfer completely.

A Pension Clearance Certificate (PCC) proves your employer is compliant with the Pension Reform Act. Employers need it for government contracts and tax incentives. You can apply online through the PenCom portal. Processing takes 5-10 working days.

The Personal Pension Plan (PPP) is a voluntary pension scheme for self-employed individuals and informal sector workers. You can contribute as little as N500 monthly. Register through the PPP portal or visit any licensed PFA to open a PPP account.

You can access pension benefits at age 50 upon retirement. If you lose your job before 50, you can access 25% of your RSA balance after 4 months of unemployment. Benefits are paid as lump sum, programmed withdrawals, or annuity based on your choice.

The Micro Pension Scheme targets small business owners, artisans, and self-employed workers. It offers flexible contributions starting from N100 per day or N500 monthly. Enroll through any licensed PFA or the online Micro Pension portal.

Employers must contribute 10% of employee monthly emoluments (with employees contributing 8%). Contributions must be remitted within 7 days of salary payment. Use the Pension Contribution Remittance System (PCRS) for online remittance.

Pencare is PenCom's health insurance program for retirees under the CPS. It provides access to quality healthcare through accredited health maintenance organizations (HMOs). Enroll through the Pencare portal at pencare.pencom.gov.ng.

To file a complaint, use the Report Employer feature on our website, visit any PenCom zonal office, or email complaints@pencom.gov.ng. Include your RSA PIN, employer name, and detailed description of the issue. PenCom investigates all complaints within 14 working days.

Does my RSA PIN change if I change jobs?
No. Your RSA PIN stays the same for life. Give it to each new employer so your contributions keep going into the same account.

What is the difference between programmed withdrawal and an annuity?
Programmed withdrawal pays you regular amounts from your RSA through your PFA. An annuity is bought from a life insurer with your RSA balance and pays you for the rest of your life.
Can retirees transfer to another PFA?
Yes, if you are on programmed withdrawal, or on annuity while making voluntary contributions.

Which employers must join the scheme?
Federal, FCT, State and Local Government employers, and private organisations with three or more employees.
How much must I contribute for each employee?
At least 10% of the employee’s monthly pay, plus the 8% you deduct from the employee: 18% in total, paid to the employee’s Pension Fund Custodian.
